manifest.name: Example Music Content Pack
manifest.description: A sample pack demonstrating the muse-ician import format: one manifest, one preset, one song, one content idea and one metadata package. Every value is placeholder data.
manifest.author: Example Author
manifest.notes:
HOW TO USE THIS TEMPLATE WITH AN AI TOOL

1. Paste this entire file and the muse-ician schema (muse-ician.schema.json) into your AI tool, or use the "Copy AI import prompt" button in the app.
2. Ask for one or more presets, songs, content ideas or metadata packages that follow this exact structure.
3. The AI may generate: preset fields (title, summary, description, objectives, platforms, duration_seconds, difficulty, budget, filming_methods, face_visibility, equipment, tags, campaign_stage, hook_examples, execution_steps, shot_list, on_screen_text, audio_guidance, editing_notes, cta_examples, variations, common_mistakes, accessibility_notes, example_metadata), plus song, content_idea and metadata_package fields.
4. The AI must NOT invent live trends, engagement statistics, view counts, sources, dates for trend evidence, or verified facts about real people. Use null or omit optional fields instead.
5. Records are linked by id. Content ideas reference songs with song_id and presets with source_preset_id. Metadata packages reference content ideas with content_idea_id. References to ids that do not exist in the file are flagged on import, not invented.
6. Keep schema_version "1.0.0" and a manifest. Return only JSON — no Markdown fences, no commentary.
7. Placeholder values in this file are marked PLACEHOLDER or is_demo: true. Replace them before using the file for real work.

Animated kinetic typography without any footage
Lyric painted on a wall, camera pulls back to reveal the room
common_mistakes: Choosing a lyric that needs the verse to make sense
Text so small or fast that people cannot read it
Illustrating the lyric literally and killing the metaphor

presets.title: Placeholder preset — copy this shape
presets.summary: PLACEHOLDER DATA — one sentence describing the video format. Replace this with a real format before using the pack.
presets.description: Pick a single line that can stand alone as a sentence. Everything in the video exists to make that line land harder: a slow reveal, a visual metaphor that matches its meaning, and text timing that lets the viewer read before the vocal arrives. Choose the lyric people quote back at you — the one with a specific image or a sharp turn of phrase, not the most repetitive hook.
presets.song_context_required: One self-contained lyric line plus the timestamp where it is sung.
hook_examples: This line took me four months to write
One lyric from the song, no explanation
The line nobody has noticed yet
execution_steps: Choose one lyric that makes sense without the surrounding verse.
Plan the visual to support the line rather than illustrate it literally.
Open with one second of quiet — an empty frame or the lyric typed out.
Split the lyric into two beats: setup, then the turn of the phrase.
Time the text so the last word arrives exactly with the vocal.
Hold the final frame for one second so viewers can screenshot it.
shot_list: Cold open: still frame or slow pan, no text
Text beat 1: first half of the lyric
Text beat 2: the turn of the line, over the musical swell
Final frame: full lyric, legible, held
presets.audio_guidance: Use the studio vocal, not a live capture. Start 1.5 seconds before the lyric so the phrase has room to arrive.
presets.editing_notes: One typeface, two sizes. Text should appear on the beat of the vocal, not before it. Keep animatics under 200ms.
cta_examples: Which line of the song hits hardest for you?
Screenshot this one and send it to whoever needs it.
presets.accessibility_notes: Minimum 32px equivalent text in a high-contrast colour, no serif script fonts, avoid text over busy footage.

example_metadata.caption_example: The last line of the bridge. The whole song lives or dies on this one.
